sourceSummary: Page 5. Lists things that help and things that shut a conversation down, and what to do when asked for something outside your role. It tells learners what to say, but never asks them to say anything.

keyIdeas: The job is to listen and stay within your role, not to fix grief.
Some well-meant phrases shut a conversation down.
A request outside your role is acknowledged, passed on the same day, and followed up.
analysis.threshold: Keeping the conversation open matters more than saying the right thing.
analysis.skill: Respond to a grieving family member without arguing, over-promising or stepping outside the student role.

candidates.name: A conversation in the corridor
candidates.angle: A resident's daughter asks the learner to get the scan redone. Each reply leads somewhere different, with coaching, and one path shows what over-promising costs. Good to vote through in class.
candidates.payoff: Handle a request outside their role while keeping the conversation open.
candidates.addresses: The request outside your role, and denial.

data.needs: A practitioner should check the dialogue and the escalation advice against your service's procedures.

candidates.name: What to say instead

insert.after: Things that shut a conversation down

candidates.angle: Each card shows one of the phrases that shut a conversation down. Learners think of a better reply before turning it.
candidates.payoff: Have a better phrase ready for the moments that usually go wrong.

data.needs: Check the replacement phrases suit the tone and cultural context of your placements.
